lxc_14fc44e5efd0c927.text: On busy days, Maria still reads her one page, so her habit grows.

lxc_338d7d0cc5bf9e15.text: Tom often skips his hour, so his cue and action never connect.

lxc_46b934846a3704ac.text: Small actions win because they still happen when you are tired, late, or not in the mood.

lxc_15047a795ea889d9.text: Small habits become easier when a clear cue meets one tiny action, and both are repeated in the same order every day.

lxc_c4df9538bff04df1.text: The cue tells your brain when to start.

lxc_3deb5a20c89b358f.text: The tiny action is small enough to survive busy or tired days.

lxc_fecd1f87706a94d2.text: Over weeks, often around 66 days, the action stops feeling like a decision and starts feeling normal.

lxc_317a82b0bc4eeca1.text: You do not need strong willpower; you need the same simple pattern, done again and again.
